text:
Andrew: Ran a focused profiling pass on the 16g pool this morning. Seeing sporadic p99 spikes when short requests pile up. Hypothesis: kernel selection hedging is introducing tails when the scheduler waits for bigger batches.
Tanvi: Interesting. Do you have the trace? Could be microbatches waiting for tokens that never show up.
Andrew: pasted profiler summary: p50 28ms, p95 120ms, p99 420ms (tail clusters at 350-600ms). CPU/GPU kernels switch at ~40 tokens threshold.
Leo: I'm seeing similar in perf lab. KV cache hit-rate drops for these tails — many requests are cold or small prefixes.
Kelsey: What are current scheduler params? I recall max_batch_tokens=8192, max_wait_ms=12 for this pool.
Andrew: yes. Current knob set: max_batch_tokens=8192, max_wait_ms=12. Kernel hedging enabled; kernel_hedge_delay_ms=6.
Tanvi: Proposal: gate the queue for very small sequences and lower max_wait_ms for small-token requests. E.g.
```
scheduler:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  max_wait_ms: 6
  small_seq_max_wait_ms: 2
  kernel_hedge: true
  hedging_threshold_tokens: 48
```
Ryan: Also try reducing hedging aggressiveness — hedging helps throughput but can hurt p99 when KV misses happen.
Leo: Ran a 10m A/B in perf lab with those params: throughput -3%, p95 -8%, p99 median -28% (420->300ms). KV-hit rate improved from 86% to 92% for the tested traffic pattern.
Kelsey: Nice. Any regressions on long-seq workloads? We must avoid harming large batched jobs.
Andrew: Long-seq tail unchanged in lab. The hit was mostly in 8-60 token requests hitting the hedging/queue window.
Ryan: We should also add a kernel fallback policy in runtime: if observed latency for chosen kernel > hedging_threshold_ms for 5 consecutive requests, route next 8 requests to smaller init kernel.
Tanvi: Pseudocode for fallback in runtime:
```
if kernel_latency_ms > hedging_threshold_ms for N=5:
  route_next(M=8) to small_init_kernel
```
Leo: I can add telemetry: measure per-kernel p50/p95/p99 and KV-hit by seq-length bucket (0-8,9-32,33-128).
sre-bot: alert: experiment 2438567890-ab started by Leo (perf-lab). CI hooks enabled.
Kelsey: schedule: roll to canary 10% for next 2 hours, monitor p99 and errors. If p99 improves and errors stable, expand.
Andrew: I'll own monitoring dashboard and rollback playbook. Kelsey will own canary rollout. Leo will update telemetry and add perf test to CI.
Ryan: After canary, let's run an overnight stress with synthetic small-seq bursts to validate no oscillation.
Tanvi: Also add a quick stress harness to simulate KV cold pattern: many unique prefixes.
Andrew: Good plan. I'll post results in this thread after the canary. :rocket:
